text:
Lucas Raymond has always been the Red Wing who makes the play before the play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 87th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, and the Olympics in February were more of the same: nine points for Sweden, eight of them assists.

What's different this fall is how often he's the one shooting. His own chances are up to 1.18 expected goals per 60 minutes, from 0.78 last season, and he has 52 shots in 17 games. Six goals on 6.8 expected is about right, so nothing about his finishing is inflated. If anything his line has been unlucky, scoring 2.8 fewer goals than its chances.

The production: 16 points, nine on the power play, 12 in his last ten games, even as Detroit dropped three of its last four. He's 24 with 400 NHL games behind him, and Evolving-Hockey had him 26th among 401 forwards last season while facing tough competition. Our range puts him near 80 points. The shot volume is the part to watch: if it holds, that range is too low.
headline: Lucas Raymond has started shooting
